# boldvideo CLI reference

## Install

Requires Node.js 22 or newer. End users do not need Bun or TypeScript.

```sh
npm install -g boldvideo
boldvideo --version
boldvideo --help
```

For a one-off invocation without a global install, use `npx boldvideo --help`.
This page covers the commands registered in the version named in its generated
comment. The command reference below is authoritative for that version; planned
commands are not silently presented as available.

## Authentication and keys

Create an API key in Bold under **Settings → Developer**. Do not put real keys
in shell history, scripts, source control or shared logs. To verify and store a
key, run the following in a terminal and enter the key at the hidden prompt:

```sh
boldvideo login
boldvideo whoami
```

For automation, inject `BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY` through your runner's secret store.
It takes precedence over both `--profile` and the active saved profile. Login
also accepts a key on stdin, so a secret manager can pipe it directly without
putting it in an argument. `--token` is available but exposes the key in process
arguments and potentially shell history.

Use named profiles to keep accounts separate:

```sh
boldvideo login --profile customer-demo
boldvideo profiles list
boldvideo profiles use customer-demo
boldvideo whoami --profile customer-demo
```

Login verifies the key before saving it; without `--profile`, the account slug
becomes the profile name. Profiles live in `boldvideo/profiles.json` under
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `~/.config` by default, or `%APPDATA%` on Windows. On POSIX,
the directory is mode 0700 and the file is mode 0600. Treat this file as a secret.

`boldvideo logout --yes` removes the active stored profile, not an environment
key. Unset `BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY` separately. Removing the active profile leaves no
active default; it does not switch to another account. Revocation of a leaked
key must happen in Bold, not just by removing the local copy.

Authenticated commands use the resolved key; admin commands require an admin
key. Help, version, login, local profile management and docs work without a key.
`BOLDVIDEO_API_URL` overrides `https://app.boldvideo.io/api/v1`; use it only for
a trusted server because authenticated requests send the key there. The OpenAPI
schema is at `https://app.boldvideo.io/api/openapi`.

`boldvideo docs cli` renders the installed command reference offline. Other docs
topics require network access; `BOLDVIDEO_DOCS_URL` overrides the docs origin
(`https://docs.boldvideo.com`). Documentation requests never send API credentials.

## Output and safety contract

- Success is one JSON value on stdout when piped or when `--json` is passed;
  terminals receive readable text or tables. IDs are never truncated.
- Exception: `boldvideo docs <topic>` prints raw markdown even when piped.
  Use `--json` for an object with `url`, `title` and `markdown` instead.
- Lists accept `--limit` (default 20) and `--fields` (comma-separated or repeated).
  A page is `{ "items": [], "has_more": false }`; when more exists, `has_more`
  is true and `next` contains the exact command for the next page. Follow it
  explicitly; the CLI does not silently fetch the whole library.
- Errors are one JSON object on nonterminal stderr: `code`, `message`, `hint`,
  `docs`, and `request_id` when available. Terminal errors show the same fields
  as text. `--json` affects success output, not stderr formatting.
- Progress and continuation hints go to terminal stderr only. `--debug` never
  dumps API keys. Nonempty `NO_COLOR` disables color; pipes never receive ANSI
  color escapes.
- Every write supports `--dry-run`. Destructive commands require `--yes` when
  stdin is not a terminal, including previews (`--dry-run --yes`). Preview first
  and check the target account with `boldvideo whoami` before applying a write.
- Ingest commands, when registered, expose `--wait`. Imports deduplicate on
  source URL so rerunning an import is safe.

To discover the exact installed surface as structured data:

```sh
boldvideo help --json
```

## Commands

### boldvideo

Run your Bold video library.

```sh
boldvideo <command> [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| --help | boolean | false | Show command help. |
| --json | boolean | false | Print JSON, even on a terminal. |
| --debug | boolean | false | Enable diagnostics on terminal stderr; never print API keys. |
| --profile | string | — | Use a stored profile for this call; BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY takes precedence. |
| --version | boolean | false | Print the installed version. |

### boldvideo login

Verify an API key and save it as the active profile.

Create keys in Bold: Settings → Developer. Omit --token to read stdin or prompt without echo. --profile names the saved profile; otherwise use the account slug. BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY still overrides saved profiles.

```sh
boldvideo login [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| --help | boolean | false | Show command help. |
| --json | boolean | false | Print JSON, even on a terminal. |
| --debug | boolean | false | Enable diagnostics on terminal stderr; never print API keys. |
| --profile | string | — | Use a stored profile for this call; BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY takes precedence. |
| --dry-run | boolean | false | Preview the write without making changes. |
| --yes | boolean | false | Confirm a destructive operation. |
| --token | string | — | API key to verify and store; omit to read it privately. |

#### Examples

Enter a key privately, or supply it through stdin.

```sh
boldvideo login
```

Verify a key and activate a named profile.

```sh
boldvideo login --token bold_demo_key_2026 --profile customer-demo
```

### boldvideo whoami

Show the authenticated account, key kind and profile.

A null profile means BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY supplied the key. The API base URL comes from BOLDVIDEO_API_URL or the Bold production default.

```sh
boldvideo whoami [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| --help | boolean | false | Show command help. |
| --json | boolean | false | Print JSON, even on a terminal. |
| --debug | boolean | false | Enable diagnostics on terminal stderr; never print API keys. |
| --profile | string | — | Use a stored profile for this call; BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY takes precedence. |

#### Examples

```sh

```

Inspect a named profile without switching the default.

```sh
boldvideo whoami --profile customer-demo --json
```

### boldvideo logout

Remove the active stored profile and its key.

--profile removes that profile instead. Environment variables are unchanged; unset BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY separately. Removing the active profile leaves no active profile.

```sh
boldvideo logout [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| --help | boolean | false | Show command help. |
| --json | boolean | false | Print JSON, even on a terminal. |
| --debug | boolean | false | Enable diagnostics on terminal stderr; never print API keys. |
| --profile | string | — | Use a stored profile for this call; BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY takes precedence. |
| --dry-run | boolean | false | Preview the write without making changes. |
| --yes | boolean | false | Confirm a destructive operation. |

#### Examples

Remove the active stored key.

```sh
boldvideo logout --yes
```

Preview removing a named profile.

```sh
boldvideo logout --profile customer-demo --dry-run --yes
```

### boldvideo docs

List documentation topics or print a page as markdown.

Resolve an exact topic, then a unique prefix or substring. The cli topic renders the installed command tree offline, without network requests. Other topics require network access. Pages print raw markdown even when piped; --json returns &#123;url, title, markdown&#125;. BOLDVIDEO_DOCS_URL overrides https://docs.boldvideo.com. Requests time out after 10 seconds and never send API credentials.

```sh
boldvideo docs [topic] [flags]
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| topic | No | Documentation topic or match. |

#### Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| --help | boolean | false | Show command help. |
| --json | boolean | false | Print JSON, even on a terminal. |
| --debug | boolean | false | Enable diagnostics on terminal stderr; never print API keys. |
| --profile | string | — | Use a stored profile for this call; BOLDVIDEO_API_KEY takes precedence. |
| --limit | number | 20 | Maximum items to return (positive integer). |
| --fields | list | — | API fields to include, comma-separated or repeated. |
| --search | string | — | Filter topics, titles and descriptions by substring. |
| --offset | number | 0 | Start at this topic (nonnegative integer). |

#### Examples

Find documentation about API authentication.

```sh
boldvideo docs --search authentication
```

Read the quickstart without leaving the shell.

```sh
boldvideo docs guides/quickstart
```

## Recipes

The three video workflows below depend on sibling command branches. They are
not executable in this reference's current base: it registers auth, profiles,
help and docs, but not videos, insights, import or ask. No speculative flags or
unsupported command lines are supplied. After those commands merge, replace
these pending workflows with parser-checked shell recipes and regenerate the
page before publishing a release. `jq` is needed for the list pipeline.

Check the installed commands before starting:

```sh
boldvideo help --json
boldvideo whoami
```

### Bulk-edit from a list pipeline

Pending `videos list` and `videos update`. Request a bounded page with only the
IDs and fields needed to select videos. Pipe the JSON `items` through `jq` to
select IDs, then loop over the IDs with quoted arguments and preview each update
using `--dry-run`. Review the previews before applying the same updates. Follow
the exact `next` command if another page exists; do not assume the first page is
the entire library.

### Weekly questions digest

Pending `insights questions`. Request questions from the last seven days, save
the JSON response to a dated file and format the returned questions into a
digest. Follow pagination when present. Schedule the read-only invocation in
your own weekly job with a secret-injected key; do not put a key in the job's
command line or digest.

### Import a channel and ask

Pending `import youtube` and `ask`. Import the channel
`https://www.youtube.com/@takimoore` into a collection and wait for ingest to
finish with `--wait`. Then ask “What does Taki say about paid workshops versus
free webinars?” scoped to that collection. Reruns deduplicate by source URL;
waiting avoids asking before content is ready.

## Exit codes

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | General failure |
| 2 | Usage error |
| 3 | Not authenticated or not permitted |
| 4 | Not found |
| 5 | Timed out while waiting |

Check the process exit status before parsing a success response. Exit 3 covers
both missing/invalid authentication and insufficient permissions. HTTP 404 maps
to exit 4; HTTP 408/504 and wait deadlines map to exit 5. Other API failures use
exit 1. Errors include a stable code and a next-command hint on stderr; scripts
should branch on the exit status or code, not the human-readable message.

```sh
boldvideo help exit-codes --json
```
